Cross-Platform Builds > FreeBSD Cross-Compilation

FreeBSD Cross-Compilation

FreeBSD is the only target that needs a “separately prepared sysroot”, for three reasons: Zig 0.17.0 does not officially publish a FreeBSD host binary; it does not bundle the freebsd libc; and zig build has no --sysroot parameter. For this, build.zig gained two generic options:

OptionEffect
-Dsysroot=<directory>Sets b.sysroot and forwards --sysroot to all compilation steps
-Dlibc=<file>Sets b.libc_file and forwards -libc (the libc installation description file)

One-Command Build (Recommended)

# 运行目录：sci 仓库根目录
sh tools/build_freebsd.sh
# 产物在 zig-out-freebsd/；可选参数：
#   --target x86_64-freebsd --prefix <输出目录> --sysroot <已有 sysroot>

On its first run the script automatically downloads the FreeBSD 14.4-RELEASE base.txz (about 155M), extracts it as a sysroot, and generates the libc description file (include_dir / sys_include_dir / crt_dir pointing at the corresponding paths inside the sysroot). Afterwards it reuses them and does not download again.

Manual Build

# 运行目录：sci 仓库根目录
SYSROOT=/tmp/fbsd/sysroot   # base.txz 解压目录，含 usr/include/stdlib.h
printf 'include_dir=%s/usr/include\nsys_include_dir=%s/usr/include\ncrt_dir=%s/usr/lib\nmsvc_lib_dir=\nkernel32_lib_dir=\ngcc_dir=\n' \
  "$SYSROOT" "$SYSROOT" "$SYSROOT" > /tmp/fbsd/libc.txt
zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-freebsd -Dllvm=false \
  -Dsysroot="$SYSROOT" -Dlibc=/tmp/fbsd/libc.txt -p zig-out-freebsd
file zig-out-freebsd/bin/sa
# 期望：ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64, for FreeBSD 14.4, interpreter /libexec/ld-elf.so.1

Native FreeBSD Build (Alternative Route)

On a FreeBSD host, build natively with the ports Zig (pkg install zig), with no sysroot needed: just zig build. But sa_std.zig contains Linux-specific code (io_uring/epoll, etc.), so real-hardware behavior still needs item-by-item verification.

The FreeBSD Compatibility Layer in sa_std.zig

All of the following are gaps in the Zig 0.17 standard library for freebsd; they are isolated in src/runtime/sa_std.zig with comptime builtin.os.tag == .freebsd branches and do not affect other platforms:

  • TCP_NODELAY: std.posix.TCP is void on freebsd, so the constant 1 is written directly (the same value on Linux/macOS/FreeBSD);
  • hostname / os_release: std.posix.uname() is void on freebsd, so it calls the libc uname instead (the FreeBSD struct utsname has five fields of 256 bytes each);
  • IP literal parsing: Address.resolveIp and Ip6Address.resolve both ultimately reach the unimplemented if_nametoindex; on freebsd an in-file numeric parser is used instead (including :: compression and embedded IPv4), while named zones use FreeBSD libc's own if_nametoindex to keep behavior equivalent; the parser has unit tests and matches the std parser byte for byte on 9 groups of vectors.
